checks.claim: C1: F1 sets up a well-formed compact indexed family with a common unit trial and a uniform epsilon. Sigma is an index, not physical time. F = E + R^2 and the frozen-coefficient flow P_sigma(t) are the actual ones. The Teschl 2014 second-edition imports (10.2 p258, conditional 10.13 p273, 4.12/4.13 pp140-141 with the H1 form domain) are scoped correctly. No all-strength binding of a fixed d3 potential is claimed.
checks.reason: The title page reads SECOND EDITION, GSM 157. The copyright page shows ISBN 978-1-4704-1704-8 and (c) 2009, 2014. Thm 10.2 (p258) covers real V in L^inf_inf + L^2 for n<=3; V=-V_sigma is bounded with compact support, so H_sigma is self-adjoint on H2, bounded below, sigma_ess=[0,inf), and C_c^inf is a core. Thm 10.13 (p273) is explicitly conditional ('If E0=min sigma(H) is an eigenvalue'), as the target says. p141 has Thm 4.12 with the remark that the quadratic form domain may replace D(A), and Cor 4.13 (A>=B implies E_n(A)>=E_n(B)). The frozen flow is the Section 7 deterministic base of the fixed-mask note with h(r)=V_sigma, which is admissible because V_sigma is in C_c^inf(K_x), and g=0. Its B(h)(e,c)=(0,h(e1+c1)) splits into the E-part plus D_sigma c=(0,V_sigma c1). M<inf follows from continuity on the compact I. F1 and the Boundaries state that sigma is an index and that no fixed-potential all-strength binding is asserted.

checks.claim: C2: F2 claims uniform existence of an isolated simple a.e.-positive ground state, E2 with threshold 0, -M<=E1<E2<=0, energy-Lipschitz bounds in ||V-V'||_inf, L2/H2 continuity of p_sigma, a gap Delta>0, sqrt(eps)<=lambda<=sqrt(M), d0>0, and the global-E complementary bound C(1+t)e^{mu t}. Only the growing branch is removed, mu=0 is handled, and no p in L1, tail estimate or d1 ODE is assumed.
checks.reason: The trial gives <w,H_sigma w> <= -eps < 0 = inf sigma_ess, so E1 is a discrete eigenvalue. 10.13 then gives simplicity and a.e.-positivity. Since V_sigma >= 0, H_sigma >= -M. Simplicity makes E2 either a strictly larger eigenvalue or the threshold 0 > E1. The bound -||V_s-V_t||_inf <= H_s - H_t <= ||V_s-V_t||_inf, combined with Cor 4.13 applied to constant shifts, gives the Lipschitz energy bound for j=1,2 using threshold-0 levels. This is Lipschitz in ||V-V'||_inf, not automatically in sigma, and the target says so. Continuity of V_sigma in L^inf makes E2-E1 continuous and positive on the compact I, so Delta>0. Then d0 >= Delta/(2 sqrt M). L2 continuity follows from norm-continuity of the Riesz projection, with the sign fixed by <p_s,p_t> > 0. H2 continuity follows from Delta p = -(E1+V)p. The global-E bound follows the old d1 method, which is dimension-free. Set A=H_sigma+1+M and B=1-Delta. Then B<=A<=(1+M)B, and the resolvent square-root comparison applies. Scalar wave entries on [-mu^2,inf) with S_t(0)=t cover mu=0. The decaying branch (p,-lambda p) evolves by e^{-lambda t}. ell^E is (1,0) on the two branches, and the pairing of p with H^{-1/2} is legitimate since p is in H2. Constants depend only on M, eps and Delta. The target labels the old note as a method comparator to be re-proved and the R^d deductions as obligations.

The functional ell = ell^E + f(c1/lambda + c2/lambda^2) gives ell(e)=1, a rank-one projection, two-sided commutation e^{lambda t}, continuity, uniform positive entrance at e0 and O_phi positivity. The full-F complement is bounded by C(1+t)^3 e^{mu t}, with an eta<d0 normalized bound. There is a finite-T0 parameter bound in ||.||_inf + ||.||_2.
checks.reason: Hand computation with ell^E P^E(s)=e^{lambda s} ell^E and ell^E(D c)=f c1 gives ell(P(t)(0,c)) = f[c1(e^{lt}-1)/l + c2(e^{lt}-1-lt)/l^2 + (c1+tc2)/l + c2/l^2] = e^{lt} f(c1/l + c2/l^2). Also ell(e_sigma) = (1+lambda/lambda)/2 = 1. f>0 because the trial forces V_sigma nonzero, V_sigma>=0 is continuous, and p>0 a.e. V p is in L1 from compact support and p in L2, so no p in L1 is needed. ell(e0)=f/lambda, and O_phi(e_sigma)=<p,phi> > 0. Both are continuous on I, so their infima are positive. For the complement: Q(ie)=iQ^E e. On constants, the Pi^E-forcing response minus e^{lt}ell(0,c)e equals -f((c1+tc2)/l + c2/l^2)e^E, which is polynomial. The Q^E-forcing part is <= int C(1+t-r)e^{mu(t-r)}||V||_2(1+r)|c| dr <= C(1+t)^3 e^{mu t}. Then (1+t)^3 e^{-(l-mu)t} <= C_eta e^{-eta t} for eta<d0. Duhamel with ||B(V)||_{F->E} <= ||V||_inf + ||V||_2 (note eq. (4)) and uniform finite-horizon bounds give the T0 parameter estimate. This is correctly stated as parameter continuity, not time-norm continuity. The 36 exact finite cases reproduce entrance beta/(2 lambda^2) and wrong-projection defect beta/(2 lambda) (e.g. lambda=2, beta=1 gives 1/8 and 1/4).

The full H:homog ranges are kept. h_sigma is the actual raw linear CM mean, q_avg is nonzero C_c^inf, and 0<Q(q_avg)<=v_Psi<inf. h_sigma >= Gamma*q_avg holds for every sigma in [0,1]. checks.reason: The ranges (d=1,2,3; a in (0,1); 0<alpha<d or alpha=d=1; alpha+a<2) match the original H:homog excerpt (lines 135-154), with a=alpha_0. h_sigma is E[W-dot(sigma,x)Z] for Cov=|s-t|^{-a}gamma(x-y). It is identical to the old consumer's (1), and q_avg and Z=W(Psi) are defined as in the old excerpt. Since |sigma-u|<=1 on [0,1]^2 and a>0, |sigma-u|^{-a}>=1, so positive Tonelli gives h_sigma >= Gamma*q_avg at the endpoints too. Integrating Psi against this gives v_Psi = int int Psi h >= int q_avg(Gamma*q_avg) = Q(q_avg). Positivity: Gamma nonzero charges some B_r, and Gamma(B_r)=r^{d-alpha}Gamma(B_1), so every ball about 0 is charged. Together with int q_avg^2>0 and continuity of q_avg*q_avg~ this gives Q>0. Finiteness follows from local finiteness. Smoothness: extend G(u,x)=(Gamma*Psi(u,.))(x) by zero in u; this is smooth because supp_t Psi is compact in (0,1). Then h_sigma = int|v|^{-a}G(sigma-v,x)dv, so sigma-derivatives fall on G, never on |.|^{-a}. This gives smoothness and Lipschitz continuity into C^k(B_{2R}). Nonzero-ness of m_R h_sigma needs R large (Gamma*q_avg>0 near supp q_avg), and the target says 'sufficiently large'.
